Koszalin Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Koszalin, Poland

Not demolished. Koszalin's earliest Jewish residents buried their dead in Szczecinek or Popielewo before this cemetery was likely established in the mid-18th century; a document from 1752 mentions a local Jewish gravedigger. It also served the Jewish community of Sianów, documented elsewhere in this collection, ten kilometers away. Devastated on Kristallnacht in November 1938, the cemetery's sole intact surviving matzevah — commemorating David Baruch (1840–1879) — was discovered by Koszalin photographer Zdzisław Pacholski in a nearby river in 2000; after a period in the Koszalin Museum, it was returned to the cemetery in 2005, when the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage in Poland undertook the site's cleanup and fencing.
